Hi Maya / WellPath procurement team,

Thanks for the time yesterday. Attaching the current Order Form (OrderForm_v3.pdf) and a short summary of the changes we made following legal's review. High level asks from your side (SOC 2 report, pen-test windows, evidence cadence) were clear — below is a proposed approach so we can close the commercial piece and get legal/security aligned.

Proposed high-level:
- Order form: we will issue a new order form with the committed capacity and start date if you confirm the attachment.
- MSA redlines: Markus is looping in legal to propose narrow language for audit rights and pen-test access (see cc).
- Evidence runway: propose a 2-week handoff window for evidence prior to any scheduled pen-test (we suggested Oct 5 for evidence handoff if pen test targets week of Oct 18).

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm that SOC 2 Type II (most recent report) can be shared under NDA.
2) Confirm preferred pen-test weeks and any blackout dates for staging.
3) Any procurement PO or contract routing requirements we should know about.

Attaching: OrderForm_v3.pdf. I'll follow up with Markus' redlines on the MSA tomorrow.

Thanks,

Thanks Ben — appreciate the proposal. Quick answers and a few clarifying asks from security: 

- SOC 2: we can share the most recent SOC 2 Type II under our standard NDA; can you send the NDA link?
- Pen test timing: we prefer non-production window weeks; target weeks we can offer in October are week of Oct 18 or Oct 25. Staging is available but will require a short onboarding checklist.
- Audit rights: our legal team is ok with bounded inspection but will need to see the specific MSA language you propose for frequency and scope.
- Evidence cadence: we generally expect a single evidence bundle + 2 follow-up clarifications; acceptable handoff is 10 business days before the test.

I've attached a spreadsheet (WellPath_Security_Questions.xlsx) with fields that our security reviewers want filled out (sample artifacts, data retention answers, encryption at rest keys). Please have your security/engineering team fill the columns.

Maya Singh

Thanks, Maya — good list. Sharing our proposed MSA redlines focused only on audit rights and inspection scope (attached: MSA_Redlines_v2.docx). Key points in the redlines: 

1) Bounded inspection: we propose language that limits inspection to a predefined scope (SOC 2, configuration screenshots, host-level pen-test results) and requires a minimum 10 business days' notice. This avoids open-ended access requests.

Suggested snippet (for your counsel to consider):
"Customer may conduct a single bounded inspection per rolling 12-month period, limited to specified SOC 2 controls and documented artifacts; any on-site or staging access shall be scheduled with a minimum of ten (10) business days' prior written notice and subject to reasonable security and data access controls"

2) Pen-test coordination: Redwood will accept customer-initiated vulnerability scans and third-party tests where the scope is limited to Redwood-managed environments for the contracted service. We ask that WellPath provide an agreed test window and pre-test checklist; Redwood will provide a single contact and ephemeral staging credentials where applicable.

3) Evidence cadence: we push for a single primary evidence handoff plus two follow-ups (clarification only). If additional discovery beyond clarifications is required, parties will negotiate a mutually-agreed scope and reasonable time/cost.

Questions for WellPath:
- Is the 10-business-day evidence runway acceptable? Maya noted 10 as acceptable — confirming.
- Any internal constraints on the number of evidence requests after the initial handoff? We suggest limiting to 2 clarifications.

Ben — I'll inline the redline file. If WellPath legal can review the snippet above and accept or propose edits, we can lock the order form and proceed to signature.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Hi Maya / team — Priyom from legal/assurance here. Reviewed Markus' redlines and the evidence expectations. We're comfortable with the bounded inspection phrasing above with two small clarifications to reduce operational friction: 

1) Evidence examples: to avoid back-and-forth, please confirm three representative artifacts we should include in the primary handoff (we recommend: redacted SOC 2 report, pen-test summary + IPs tested, and a short runbook for staging onboarding).
2) Staging access: we will provide ephemeral credentials scoped to non-prod and will require a time-box (24–72 hours) per access window. Please confirm that your testers can operate within that time-box.

If you confirm those two items by EOD Oct 5 we will accept the redline language and proceed to signature. Attaching a short evidence-runbook-stub.pdf to show typical items we plan to hand over.
